summary: Named 77 of 77 FUN_XXXX functions in wtrea.ovr (plus 1 dispatch entry at 0x0e that Ghidra missed, manually created and named — total 78 names applied) (TREA = treasure: post-combat loot rolls, chest-interaction UI, trap-identification + disarm, chest-spell casting, and the loot-distribution UI). wtrea.ovr is a TRUE state-machine handler (like wmele/wbase/wpcvw) covering states `0x0f` (post-combat treasure pickup) and `0x15` (in-dungeon chest encounter), both transitioning back to state `0x16` on return. The state handlers share `wtrea_run_loot_rolls` at 0x509d which executes 6 weighted die rolls against a per-encounter-difficulty loot-table indexed by `*0x43c4` (the treasure-class word set by combat/maze code). **Flagship discoveries**: (1) the LOOT-ROLL TABLE FORMAT at `wtrea_run_loot_rolls` — 6 entries × 6 bytes each (+0..+1 base, +2..+3 dice, +4 type, +5 drop_chance%); type-1 = gold pile (rng(max-min)+min, accumulated into 32-bit gold pool), type-2 = item drop (rng(dice)+base item-id into the slot array), type-4 = XP-bonus (dice × base added unmodified per character); gold is DIVIDED by party_size via FUN_3f1e but XP is given full to each alive member; (2) the TPK TREASURE TRIGGER — if zero alive party members when treasure rolls (because monsters wiped them just before this overlay loaded), wtrea writes `*0x363a=8` to force the graveyard-recovery state via winit.ovr (so the treasure is effectively forfeit); (3) the FAMOUS WIZ6 TRAP-DISARM FORMULA at `wtrea_action_disarm_trap` (0x2582): `score = thief_skill_byte/2 + dex/2 + level - chest_difficulty*2`, plus class bonus (Thief +dex*3, Ninja/Bard/class-13 +dex*2), clamped 5..0x5f (95 max), rolled against rng(100); 3-way outcome (clean disarm, miss, CRITICAL-FAIL where the trap auto-triggers) — and CRITICAL-FAIL is taken when `roll > 100 - (100-score)/3` OR when the player misidentifies the trap type, so misidentifying a high-DC trap is essentially always-fail; (4) the TRAP-NAME SELECTION ALGORITHM at `wtrea_select_trap_type` (0x214d): cycles a 16-bit `*0x5192` index 0..15 (wraps), decrementing a starting rng(100) count each time the per-chest-tier trap-bitmap (at loot_table+0x24) has bit `*0x5192` set, picking the bit position where the count zeroes out — so traps available in more chest tiers get rolled more often, with the per-cycle cap of 100 iterations guaranteeing termination; (5) the PROGRESSIVE TRAP REVEAL at `wtrea_progressive_trap_reveal` (0x21c9) — the 'Calfo / Inspect' identify mechanic; per call adds successful-reveal characters from the actual trap name (color 6 = white) and `rng(26) + 'A'` decoy characters (color 12 = dark/red) into a display buffer at *0x51bc, so multiple inspect attempts gradually reveal more of the trap's letters while seeding decoys to confuse; (6) the CHEST-SPELL-CAST UI at `wtrea_action_cast_chest_spell` (0x3406, 2687 bytes — largest in the overlay): two-stage menu where the player first picks 1 of 6 spell schools (filtered against the character's spell-known bitmap at +0x4570 via `wtrea_filter_known_spells_in_school` 0x32eb scanning 82 spells), then picks a specific spell + power level (1..6, capped at (caster_level - spell_base_level + 1)), with mana check at `+0x4410 + school*4` (6 schools × 4 bytes = 24-byte mana array), spell-cost = base_byte * power_level; (7) embeds a stripped-down 3D dungeon RENDERER at `wtrea_render_3d_view` (0x6c8f, 2192 bytes) so the dungeon view stays visible behind the chest dialog — same architecture as wmnpc's embedded renderer.
method: PyGhidra + DecompInterface for all 77 functions in wtrea.ovr (BinaryLoader, file_offset == Ghidra address). For each function: (a) decompiled C, (b) outgoing intra-overlay CALL edges, (c) cross-overlay thunk calls (any 'call_internal' target >= 0xB000 that isn't in our function set). 45 distinct thunks resolved via the thunk-delta law (bss_offset - 0xBA9C = wroot file offset); cross-referenced against wroot-naming-pass.json + informal names from wpcvw/wpcmk/wmele/wmaze/wbase/wmnpc passes (merged 91 informal thunk names). Names applied when multi-signal evidence converged: BSS field offsets (character record at +0x43e8 stride 0x1b0 reused from wpcvw — inventory slots at +0x4428 main + +0x442f flags including 0x40 cursed-on-equip, gold at +0x43fc, XP at +0x43f4, mana per-school at +0x4410+school*4, skill bytes at +0x451c+skill_idx, condition resistance at +0x453a+condition_idx, class at +0x4587), thunk-call vocabularies (window create/focus/clear/redraw, msg load+print, rng_next, play_sound, kbd polling, mouse, getbit_test), trap/disarm idiom recognition (skill/2 + dex/2 + level - difficulty*2 formula), loot-roll structure (6×6 table with type-byte dispatch matching the 1=gold/2=item/4=xp pattern), and indirect-call dispatcher patterns (the 5-entry chest-menu jumptable at CS:-0x6a1c in `wtrea_chest_menu_main`, the spell-action table at CS:0x7f62, the 14-entry wall-renderer dispatch in scene_visit_forward_cell). Dispatch entry at file 0x0e (14-byte header — same as wbase/wmele/wpcvw) was not auto-detected by Ghidra; we created it as part of this pass. Confirmed wtrea is a STATE-MACHINE HANDLER by grep showing `833e 3a36 0f` (cmp word [0x363a], 0xf) at 0x26 and `833e 3a36 15` at 0x38 — both write `*0x363a=0x16` and call their respective sub-handlers.

states_handled.purpose: Post-combat treasure pickup. Entered from wmele.ovr when combat ends with treasure pending (`*0x43c4` holding the treasure-class index). Opens windows, loads strings, calls `wtrea_run_loot_rolls`. On return, writes `*0x363a=0x16` (transition to wherever 0x16 leads — likely back to wmaze or to the next sub-state).

In-dungeon chest encounter (player walked into a chest tile). Slightly different UI mode (`*0x50c8=1` vs `=2` for state 0xf) but shares `wtrea_run_loot_rolls`. Increments a per-encounter chest counter at *0x4ee8 (likely 'chests-opened-this-session' for stats). Sub-state in `*0x4fce` set to 0x15 for nested screen tracking.

state_machine.dispatch_entry: 0x0e (14-byte overlay header; Ghidra did NOT auto-detect this function — we created it as part of this pass)
transitions_out: state 0x16 (22): written at end of dispatch for either 0x0f or 0x15 — looks up the next overlay to handle state 0x16. We have not yet identified which overlay claims state 0x16 (candidate next-step after treasure: possibly wbase main menu or wmaze).
state 8 (graveyard): written by `wtrea_run_loot_rolls` at 0x509d when the alive-party-member count is zero (post-combat TPK scenario). Yields to winit.ovr graveyard handler.
sub_state_writes: *0x43c4 = 0xffff set by `wtrea_run_loot_rolls` after rolling treasure (marks treasure as consumed)

key_discoveries: **LOOT-ROLL TABLE FORMAT at `wtrea_run_loot_rolls` (0x509d)** — Wiz6's treasure rolling is a single 6-entry table loaded via `data_table_load(7, buf, *0x43c4, 0)` where each entry is 6 bytes: (+0..+1 base, +2..+3 dice, +4 type, +5 drop_chance%). Each iteration: roll `rng(100)`; if `roll < drop_chance` then dispatch on type byte: **type 1 (GOLD)** rolls `rng(max - min) + min` and adds to 32-bit gold accumulator (local_7e); **type 2 (ITEM)** rolls `rng(dice) + base` and stores in the item slot array at *0x51d6 (up to 9 items per chest, count in *0x5266); **type 4 (XP-BONUS)** does `local_82 += base * dice`. After all rolls: count alive members (slot+0x4589 == 0); if zero → force state 8 (graveyard); else FUN_3f1e divides the 32-bit gold by party_size and gives EACH alive member `gold/N` (with carry) into `+0x43fc`, AND adds the FULL xp_bonus to each member's `+0x43f4`. Then if item drops exist, invokes the loot-distribution UI. Important: the 32-bit math for gold-divide may overflow in pathological cases (party_size=0 would div-by-zero, but the alive-count check prevents this). XP is GROUP — every alive member gets the full type-4 bonus, no division. The table caps at 6 entries so each chest can drop max 6 'items' (but each can be gold OR an item OR XP).

**TPK TREASURE TRIGGER → GRAVEYARD** — If `wtrea_run_loot_rolls` (0x509d) counts zero alive party members at the moment of treasure roll (because the last monster's death-attack killed the final party member during combat, but the game already queued the treasure), wtrea writes `*0x363a=8` and returns. State 8 is the graveyard / total-party-kill recovery handler in winit.ovr. **Implication**: a TPK that happens during the kill-the-last-monster moment results in the treasure being LOST — the rolled gold/items are never distributed because the loot loop bails before the per-character apply loop runs. So Wiz6 punishes losses-at-the-finish-line by forfeiting the loot that would have been earned.

**WIZ6 DISARM FORMULA — `wtrea_action_disarm_trap` (0x2582)** — The full thief disarm math reproduced from asm: `local_a = thief_skill_byte/2 + dex/2 + level - dungeon_depth*2`; class bonus: Thief (class 3) → `+= dex*3`, Ninja/Bard/class-13 (4, 6, 13) → `+= dex*2`. Clamp 5..0x5f (5..95). Roll `rng(100)`. Three outcomes: **(a)** roll < score → SUCCESS, trap disarmed; **(b)** roll > 100 - (100-score)/3 → CRITICAL FAILURE — the trap auto-triggers (function returns -1 just like a misidentification); **(c)** otherwise MISS, no progress. Crucially, if the player MISIDENTIFIES the trap (picks wrong from the displayed trap-bitmap candidates), the function returns -1 immediately without even rolling — same outcome as a critical fail. So picking the wrong trap from a long list of plausible candidates is just as bad as botching the roll. The dungeon_depth penalty (*0x363c * -2) means deep traps require either a high-level Thief or significant Dex investment. The clamp at 0x5f (95) caps even a perfect Thief at 95% success — Wiz6 deliberately denies any guaranteed disarm. Skill training at 0x14f2 lets disarm-skill train each attempt with probability `rng(skill_byte) <= level * mul` (mul=3 for Thief, 2 for Ninja/Bard) — so Thieves train disarm 50% faster than other classes.

**TRAP SELECTION ALGORITHM — `wtrea_select_trap_type` (0x214d)** — Wiz6's per-chest trap is rolled by a UNIFORM-OVER-PRESENT-BITS algorithm: read the loot table's 16-bit trap-bitmap at `param_1 + 0x24` (each bit = one trap type allowed for this chest tier); then `*0x5192 = 0; count = rng(100) + 1; while count > 0 AND iter_cap (100) NOT exceeded: *0x5192 = (*0x5192 + 1) % 16; if getbit_test(bitmap, *0x5192) == 1: count--;`. The final `*0x5192` is the chosen trap_id (1..16). Then it loads msg-id `*0x5192 + 0x14b4` (the trap-name text) into buffer 0x50ca and copies to *0x50de (the displayed trap name). The 100-iteration cap means there's a graceful fallback if the trap-bitmap is empty (the loop terminates with whatever *0x5192 ended at). Effective trap distribution: with a uniform `rng(100)+1` start and a cyclic walk, traps that appear in MORE chest tiers get rolled across more chest contexts, while traps that appear in only one tier appear consistently when that tier is rolled. This is closer to weighted-by-availability than truly random.

**PROGRESSIVE TRAP REVEAL — `wtrea_progressive_trap_reveal` (0x21c9) — the 'CALFO' mechanic** — When the player INSPECTs a chest (or casts an identify-trap spell), this function ADDS letters to a display buffer at *0x51bc (max 18 entries, count at *0x51d0). Each call has two parts: **(a) reveal**: for each existing decoy in the buffer, roll `rng(100) > 0x32` (cooldown), then `rng(100) < param_4` (skill check); on success, check if the next letter of the actual trap name is in the existing display; if not, replace the decoy with `'$'` (placeholder revealing a slot has been ID'd); **(b) augment**: while iVar4 > 0 still has reveal-slots, roll `rng(100) < param_4` (same skill check); on success, add a letter from `*0x50de` (the actual name), else add a random `rng(26) + 'A'` decoy. Letters are flagged as 'real' (color 6 = white, *0x5194[i] = 1) or 'decoy' (color 12 = darker, *0x5194[i] = 0). After ~5+ inspects the player can usually see enough real letters to guess the trap. **Player experience**: this is what makes Wiz6 trap-identification feel like a Sherlockian word-puzzle — you're not just rolling a dice, you're collecting partial-information clues across multiple inspect attempts.

**TWO-STAGE CHEST-SPELL UI — `wtrea_action_cast_chest_spell` (0x3406)** — The largest function in wtrea (2687 bytes) handles the spell-on-chest interaction. Stage 1: 6-cell spell-school selector (uVar6 0..5 for the 6 schools, plus cell 6 = cancel). For each school, calls `wtrea_filter_known_spells_in_school` (0x32eb) which iterates the 82-entry global spell table at +0xde stride 6, matching entries where `spell.category_byte (+0xde + i*6) == school_id` AND `getbit_test(char.spell_known_bitmap_at_+0x4570, i) == 1`. So the spell list per school is filtered by what the chosen character KNOWS — a non-Bishop with limited spellbook will see fewer options. Stage 2: pick specific spell + POWER LEVEL (1..6). Power-level cap is `min(6, caster_level - spell_base_level + 1)` so spells need 1 caster level over the spell's base for power-1, 2 for power-2, up to 6 for max-power. Mana cost = `spell.mana_per_power_byte (+0xe0) * power_level`; checked against `+0x4410 + school_idx*4` (the 6×4-byte mana array — supports up to 32-bit MP per school, but in practice capped much lower). If `spell.target_byte (+0xe2) == 1`, calls `wtrea_pick_party_member_target` (0x10e5) to choose target. Returns `power_level * 256 + spell_id` (packed). The 'on-chest' nature of the cast restricts the spell-school catalog to **chest-context spells** — likely identify, dispel, knock, locate, anti-mage-lock, etc.

**THE 5-ACTION CHEST MENU — `wtrea_chest_menu_main` (0x4ba1)** — The CALFO/INSPECT/DISARM/OPEN/SPELL/LEAVE menu in one place. After loading the loot table (which contains the trap-bitmap), the function reads byte +0x27 of the loot table as a chest-type flag (0=no chest, 1=type-A chest, 2=type-B chest — likely chest-tier visual variant). Then rolls `wtrea_select_trap_type` to set *0x5192 = trap_id. The menu loops over `wtrea_grid_menu_picker` (0x0c05) with a 5-entry `local_22 = {1,1,1,1,1}` enable-array — all 5 actions are always enabled. Player picks 0..4, the function dispatches via indirect-jump through CS-relative offset table at `-0x6a1c` (5 × 2-byte function pointers). Index 4 = LEAVE (exits the menu loop). Indexes 0..3 map (by elimination from the 5 functions called only via this jump): INSPECT (probably `wtrea_progressive_trap_reveal` 0x21c9 wrapped) / DISARM (0x2582) / OPEN (0x23b5 which computes the trap-success score and calls 0x21c9) / SPELL (0x3406). The exact jumptable resolution requires a runtime trace or symbol-table extraction we deferred.

**THE 6-SCHOOL × 4-BYTE MANA ARRAY at character+0x4410** — wtrea reads/writes mana at `slot*0x1b0 + school_idx*4 + 0x4410`. Each school's MP is 4 bytes (32-bit), which is far more than needed (max plausible MP < 1000). Likely 2 bytes are MP + 2 bytes are MP-max, OR there are 'spell points used' and 'spell points base' fields paired. Schools 0..5 = the 6 Wiz6 spell schools (Mage, Priest, Alchemist, Psionic, etc., depending on Wiz6 lineage). Sister field at +0x4570 is the 82-bit (=82 spells / 8 = 11 bytes? Or 82 nibbles = 41 bytes?) spell-known bitmap — read via `getbit_test(char+0x4570, spell_idx)`.

**LOOT TABLE BYTE LAYOUT** — From the analysis of `wtrea_run_loot_rolls` (0x509d) and `wtrea_chest_menu_main` (0x4ba1), the table loaded by `data_table_load(7, ...)` has at minimum: bytes +0x00..+0x17 = 6 × 4 bytes (base[0..3] and dice[0..1]) per entry — wait, that's stride 6 not 4; let me re-derive: 6 entries × 6 bytes total = 36 bytes. Layout per entry: +0 base_lo, +1 base_hi, +2 dice_lo, +3 dice_hi, +4 type_byte (1=gold, 2=item, 4=xp), +5 drop_chance%. Then at +0x24..+0x25: 16-bit trap-bitmap (which traps allowed). At +0x27: chest-type flag (0/1/2). Total table size likely 0x28 = 40 bytes per entry-set. Table-id = 7 in the data-table-load API; keyed by treasure-class index (*0x43c4) set by the encounter that triggered the treasure.

**DUNGEON-DEPTH PENALTY via *0x363c** — Both `wtrea_action_disarm_trap` (0x2582) and `wtrea_action_open_or_inspect` (0x23b5) penalize disarm/open scores by `dungeon_depth * 2` to `* 3/2` to `* 1` depending on class. *0x363c is a wmaze-managed BSS slot that holds the player's current dungeon LEVEL (depth). At level 10, a non-Thief takes -10 to disarm score; a Thief takes only -10 too (no class-modifier on this penalty). This matches Wiz6's brutal scaling — deep dungeon traps are essentially undisarmable by anyone other than a leveled-up Thief with maxed Dex. Notably, the OPEN action (which is what triggers the trap if not disarmed) ALSO uses *0x363c, scaled differently per class — Thief gets `*-2`, Ninja/Bard `*-3/2`, others `*-1`. So OPEN is least-penalizing-by-depth for non-thieves, paradoxically incentivizing 'just open it without trying to disarm' on low-level chests.

**INVENTORY-INSERT (CHEST→CHARACTER) — `wtrea_inventory_insert` (0x401f)** — Same 10-main + 12-overflow layout as wmnpc/wpcvw inventory inserts. Reads item-data via `data_table_load(1, buf, item_id, 0)`; if stackable (byte at +0xcc table == 1), rolls quantity via `*(*0x51d6+slot)*2 + 0x51e2` (per-slot pre-rolled quantity); else `roll_dice_with_base(...)`. Scans main inventory slots 0..9 for existing-stackable match (sum < 0xfb); if not found, scans overflow slots 10..21; if neither, allocates new slot (incrementing +0x4594 for main or +0x4595 for overflow). On full (22 slots taken) returns 0xffff. Cursed-flag translation: src item.flag bit 0x08 → dest 0x04 (cursed-unidentified), src 0x04 → 0x08 (cursed-identified), src 0x10 → 0x10, src 0x20 → 0x20, src 0x02 → 0x40 (class-locked). Cursed-on-equip (0x40) flag means the item CAN be put in inventory but cannot be unequipped without remove-curse — wpcvw's check `if (bVar5 & 1 || bVar5 & 2 || bVar5 & 0x40)` blocks unequip. After insert, recomputes total inventory weight by summing per-slot weight contributions via `inventory_item_weight_lookup` (0x3fc0).

**THE LOOT-DISTRIBUTION UI — `wtrea_loot_distribution_ui` (0x43ee, 1583 bytes)** — Opens two windows (item-list at 0x12x7 and item-detail at 0x12x6), iterates through *0x5266 items the chest dropped, lets the player navigate with cursor keys (L/R cursor + ENTER for select, ESC to skip), and for each item invokes `wtrea_pick_party_member_target` (0x10e5) for who gets it, then `wtrea_inventory_insert` (0x401f) to add. On inventory-full: prints msg + plays 'deny' sound 0x4970; the item stays in the chest. After the distribution loop, if any items remain with status==1 in *0x5274 (unclaimed), plays a 'leave-behind' sound. Items that the party CAN'T carry are explicitly forfeit — Wiz6 doesn't allow stashing in the dungeon. The 'first item gets large detail box; rest are small list rows' UI pattern mirrors wpcvw's inventory browser. Item-name strings live in MSG.DBS at offset 4000 + per-item-id (computed in the inner loop).

**EMBEDDED 3D DUNGEON RENDERER at `wtrea_render_3d_view` (0x6c8f, 2192 bytes)** — Like wmnpc, wtrea has its own stripped-down 3D corridor renderer so the dungeon stays visible behind the chest UI. Reads wall bitmaps at *0x4faa+0x43a / +0x49a (same layout as wmaze and wmnpc). Renders 4 forward cells with rotation by *0x4f9a (facing 0..3). 14 wall-render dispatchers (`scene_visit_*` functions 0x576f, 0x5895, 0x58fa, 0x59e0, 0x5dc9, 0x5f86, 0x6224, 0x676c, 0x695b) handle the wall/floor/door drawing. The `*0x363c` sub-state distinguishes corridor/room/chest modes (values 0/4/5/10/12 — same set as wmnpc). 8 small (~40-60 byte) clear-byte functions (0x6a4a..0x6ba0) handle per-cell visibility-byte resets for fog-of-war / occlusion logic. **Maintenance burden**: wmaze, wmnpc, AND wtrea each have their own copies of the same wall-render constants — three places to update if the 3D scene math changes.

**THE 32-BIT ARITHMETIC THUNK FUN_3f1e (wroot file 0x3f1e, thunk 0xf9ba) — used by GOLD-DIVIDE in 0x509d AND XP-BONUS-MULTIPLY in 0x5552**. Inspection of wroot's bytes shows it's a signed 32-bit operator with sign-twiddling (push di; sign-of-dx; negate ax/dx; xor sign-flag; recurse into unsigned core via 'call +0x39'; un-negate result). The wmnpc pass annotated this as 'likely 32-bit multiply'. wtrea uses it BOTH for: (a) GOLD = total_gold / party_size in 0x509d (input DX:AX = gold, BX:CX = party_size), implying it's actually 32-bit DIVIDE; AND (b) bonus calculation in 0x5552 (two consecutive calls — could be multiply chain or div+modulo). The function likely does BOTH multiply and divide depending on a flag input we haven't isolated. Promoted to wroot-naming-pass.json: `sdiv32_or_smul32_signed` (or split into two thunks if the recursive helper has a divide-vs-multiply selector).

bss_layout.topic: wtrea BSS layout — overlaps with wmaze/wmele state (the character record at 0x43e8 is shared with all overlays)
bss_layout.note: wtrea uses the same character record at 0x43e8 stride 0x1b0 used by wpcvw/wmnpc/wmele. Trap state lives in *0x5192 (trap_id), *0x50ca/0x50de (trap name buffer), *0x51bc..0x51d0 (the progressive-reveal display buffer + status flags). Loot pile lives in *0x51d6 (item-id array), *0x5266 (count), *0x51e2 (per-slot quantity), *0x51ee (per-slot name strings), and *0x5274/0x5276 (per-slot leave-behind flags). Chest sub-state in *0x363c (dungeon depth — read by disarm/open formulas).

findings.claim: wtrea.ovr has a 14-byte overlay header (bytes 0..0x0d: `f2 00 72 45 5b 75 ee 4f 2a 00 54 04 8f ba`). The function at file 0x0e is the state-machine dispatcher: bytes 0x0e..0x1d initialize 4 BSS slots (`*0x501c = 0xffff; *0x501e = 0; *0x5020 = 0xffff; *0x5022 = 0xffff`); then bytes 0x18..: `cmp word [0x363a], 0x0f; jnz +0xb; mov word [0x363a], 0x16; call 0x561c; jmp +0x18` followed by the same pattern for state 0x15 → call 0x56c5. Default (neither 0x0f nor 0x15): just write `*0x363a=0x16` and return. So wtrea handles states 0x0f and 0x15, both transitioning OUT to state 0x16.

evidence.details: Raw bytes at 0x26: `83 3e 3a 36 0f` (cmp word [0x363a],0xf), 0x2b: `75 0b` (jnz +0xb), 0x2d: `c7 06 3a 36 16 00` (mov word [0x363a],0x16), 0x33: `e8 e6 55` (call rel16 0x55e6 → after-IP 0x36 + 0x55e6 wrap = 0x561c). Same pattern at 0x38..0x4e for state 0x15 → calls 0x56c5. Then default `c7 06 3a 36 16 00 b8 00 00 c3` at 0x44..0x4d (mov state=0x16, mov ax,0, ret). Confirmed wtrea is a TRUE state-machine handler (unlike wmnpc/wpcmk which are library overlays).

findings.claim: `wtrea_run_loot_rolls` (0x509d) implements the loot-roll engine: 6 entries × 6 bytes loaded via `data_table_load(7, local_2e, *0x43c4, 0)`. Each entry has (+0..+1 base16, +2..+3 dice16, +4 type, +5 drop_chance%). Type byte values: 1=GOLD (rng(max-min)+min into 32-bit accumulator), 2=ITEM (rng(dice)+base item-id into the slot array), 4=XP-BONUS (base*dice into a 32-bit XP-bonus). Distribution: gold accumulator divided by party_size via FUN_3f1e and added per-character to +0x43fc; XP-bonus added in FULL to each alive character's +0x43f4 (no division).

evidence.details: Decompiled inner loop: `for local_4 in 0..6: roll = rng(100); if roll < drop_chance_byte: type = type_byte_of_entry; if type==1: gold_roll = rng(max-min)+min; CARRY into 32-bit local_7e; if type==2: item_id = rng(dice)+base; *(local_4*2 + 0x51d6) = item_id; if id>0: *0x5266++; if type==4: local_82 += base * dice (long)`. After loop: count alive (slot+0x4589 == 0) → local_7a; if 0: *0x363a=8 (TPK→graveyard); else: `local_7e = FUN_3f1e(local_7e, party_size)` (the 32-bit math thunk); for each item slot, look up name via `data_table_load(1, namebuf, item_id, 0)`, store at *0x51ee+slot*0x12, set quantity via `roll_dice_with_base` if stackable; then for each alive character: `*(slot*0x1b0+0x43f4) += local_82 (xp, with carry); *(slot*0x1b0+0x43fc) += local_7e (gold-per-member, with carry)`; if *0x5266 > 0, call wtrea_loot_distribution_ui (0x43ee). Confirmed by the consistent 32-bit add-with-carry pattern + the 4-byte stride access at +0x43f4 (xp) and +0x43fc (gold). The 6-iteration cap is hardcoded as `do { ... } while (local_4 < 6)`.

findings.claim: If `wtrea_run_loot_rolls` (0x509d) finds zero alive party members at distribution time, it writes `*0x363a=8` and SKIPS the distribution. State 8 is winit.ovr's graveyard / TPK recovery handler. The rolled treasure is LOST — never distributed because the loop bails before applying. So when a player wipes during the kill-the-last-monster moment, they FORFEIT the just-rolled treasure.

evidence.details: Post-roll alive-count: `local_7a = 0; for local_4 in 0..party_size: if *(local_4*0x1b0 + 0x4589) == 0: local_7a++`. Then: `if (local_7a == 0) { *0x363a = 8; } else { /* divide gold, distribute */ }`. The state-8 write bypasses every per-character accumulation. The match for state 8 is from `wroot-functions.md` / state-table — handled by winit.ovr 0xdf6 (graveyard). Confirmed by tracing the state-machine dispatch table.

findings.claim: `wtrea_action_disarm_trap` (0x2582) implements Wiz6's full thief disarm. After the player picks a trap-name candidate from the displayed candidates: if guess != *0x5192 (the actual trap), return -1 immediately (critical fail). If correct: compute `score = thief_skill_byte/2 + dex/2 + level - dungeon_depth*2`. Class bonus: Thief (3) → +dex*3, Ninja/Bard/13 (4, 6, 13) → +dex*2. Clamp 5..0x5f. Roll rng(100). Three outcomes: (a) roll < score → SUCCESS; (b) roll > 100 - (100-score)/3 OR roll > 0x5e → CRITICAL FAIL (return -1, trap auto-triggers); (c) else MISS (return 0).

evidence.details: Function body after candidate match: `if (local_2e[local_c] == *0x5192) { iVar3 = param_1 * 0x1b0; local_a = *(byte*)(iVar3+0x452b)/2 + *(byte*)(iVar3+0x4518)/2 + *(int*)(iVar3+0x440c) + *0x363c * -2; if (*(char*)(iVar3+0x4587) == 3) { local_a += dex*3; call wtrea_skill_train(...); } else if (class in {4,6,13}) { local_a += dex*2; call wtrea_skill_train(...); }; clamp(local_a, 5, 0x5f); iVar3 = rng(100); if (iVar3 < local_a) return 1; else if (100 - (100-local_a)/3 < iVar3) return -1; else return 0; } else return -1;`. The +0x452b offset = skill index 0xf within +0x451c skill array. Class 3 = Thief (per wpcvw findings). Skill-train calls 0x14f2 with skill index = 0xf, multiplier = 3 (Thief) or 2 (other).

findings.claim: `wtrea_select_trap_type` (0x214d) chooses the chest's trap via uniform-over-bits walk. Reads 16-bit trap-bitmap at loot_table_param + 0x24. Initializes *0x5192 = 0. Sets `count = rng(100) + 1`. Loops: `*0x5192 = (*0x5192 + 1) % 16; if getbit_test(bitmap, *0x5192) == 1: count--;` until count == 0 OR 100 iterations. The final *0x5192 is the trap_id (1..16, or 0 if bitmap empty). Then loads msg `0x14b4 + *0x5192` (trap name) into 0x50ca and strcpy to 0x50de.

evidence.details: Function body: `*0x5192 = 0; iVar1 = rng(100); iVar1 = iVar1 + 1; iVar3 = 0; while (iVar1 > 0 && iVar3 < 100) { *0x5192 = *0x5192 + 1; if (*0x5192 > 0xf) *0x5192 = 0; iVar3 = *0x5192; iVar2 = getbit_test(param_1+0x24, *0x5192); if (iVar2 == 1) iVar1 = iVar1 - 1; } load_msg_into_buf(*0x5192 + 0x14b4, 0x50ca); strcpy(0x50de, 0x50ca);`. The 100-iter cap + initial randomization gives roughly-uniform distribution over present bits, with small bias toward earlier-indexed traps due to the deterministic walk.

findings.claim: `wtrea_progressive_trap_reveal` (0x21c9) implements the multi-attempt INSPECT/CALFO mechanic. Each call: (a) for each existing display-slot, if rng(100) > 0x32 AND rng(100) < param_4 (skill check), try to mark a decoy as real-letter if the real trap-name has that character; (b) while loops remain, on rng(100) < param_4 add a random char from the real trap-name with flag=1 (color 6, white), else add a random decoy `rng(26) + 'A'` with flag=0 (color 12, dark). param_3 = max reveals per call. The display buffer at *0x51bc + flag array at *0x5194 accumulates state across multiple INSPECT calls.

evidence.details: Body iterates: `while (iVar4 < *0x51d0 && param_3 > 0)` for the reveal phase; then `for (; param_3 > 0; param_3--)` for the augment phase. Inside: rng(100) gate checks, `*(local_4 + 0x51bc) = char` writes, `*(local_4 * 2 + 0x5194) = 1 or 0` for the real-vs-decoy flag, and `*(local_4 + 0x50de) = 0x24 ('$')` to mark a revealed character in the source. After updates: `ui_window_box_draw + ui_window_set_cursor(param_1, 1, 2)`; if *0x5192 == 0 (no trap), just print 0x50ca; else iterate display showing each char colored by its flag (6 for real, 12 for decoy).

findings.claim: `wtrea_action_cast_chest_spell` (0x3406, 2687 bytes) is the two-stage chest-spell UI. Stage 1: 6-cell school-picker via `wtrea_render_spell_menu_window` (0x315c). For each school selection: `wtrea_filter_known_spells_in_school` (0x32eb) scans the 82-entry spell table at +0xde stride 6, picking entries where `spell.category_byte == school_id` AND `char.spell_known_bitmap_at_+0x4570` has that spell bit set. Stage 2: spell + power-level picker (1..6, capped at `min(6, level - spell.base_level + 1)`); mana check at `+0x4410 + school*4` (32-bit per school) compared against `spell.mana_per_power_byte * power_level`. Returns `power_level * 256 + spell_id` packed.

evidence.details: Two-window setup: `local_4 = ui_window_create(0, 0x12, 0x17, 7, 0x19, ..., 0)`; `local_6 = ui_window_create(0x16, 0x13, 0x12, 6, 0x1a, 0xfffb, 0, 0)`. Stage 1 loop: `do { ... show 6 cells (uVar6 = 0..5); local_8 = wmnpc_pick_dialogue_keyword(...); dispatch on cursor; on select (local_8=5 and local_c != 0): break; } while (uVar6 != 0xffff);` where local_c = wtrea_filter_known_spells_in_school(param_2, uVar6, local_34). Stage 2 (inside outer if): caps `iVar3 = min(6, level - spell.base_level + 1)` and lets player pick power level via similar cursor menu; checks mana `*(param_2 * 0x1b0 + iVar7 * 4 + 0x4410) >= mana_cost`. Final: if requires target, calls `wtrea_pick_party_member_target(0x7ee)`. Returns power<<8 | spell_id packed in iVar1.

findings.claim: Character has 82-bit spell-known bitmap at `+0x4570` (so 82/8 = ~10.25 bytes, likely padded to 11 bytes). `wtrea_filter_known_spells_in_school` (0x32eb) iterates spell-id 0..0x51 (81), looks up category byte at global table `*0xde + spell_id * 6` (so spell table stride is 6 bytes), and returns spells matching the requested school AND in the bitmap. Wiz6 spells thus fit in a single 6-byte record × 82 entries (492 bytes).

evidence.details: `local_4 = 0; for iVar2 in 0..0x52: if (*(byte*)(iVar2*6 + 0xde) == param_2): iVar1 = getbit_test(param_1*0x1b0 + 0x4570, iVar2); if (iVar1 == 1): *(int*)(param_3 + local_4*2) = iVar2; local_4++; return local_4;`. The 6-byte spell record per entry: +0..+1 likely name-msg-id, +2 likely category/school byte (the +0xde offset suggests a base of 0xde for spell-name table, with school filtering via masking), +3..+4 likely level/mana, +5 likely effect-type. With 82 spells the bitmap needs 82 bits = at least 11 bytes.

findings.claim: `wtrea_chest_menu_main` (0x4ba1) implements the 5-option chest interaction menu: INSPECT, DISARM, OPEN, SPELL, LEAVE. After `wtrea_select_trap_type` (0x214d) sets *0x5192, opens 2 windows (loot-display + menu), populates menu cells via `wtrea_putchar_at_with_attr` (0x4345) repeatedly, loops `wtrea_grid_menu_picker` (0x0c05) until selection < 5, then dispatches via CS-relative jumptable at `-0x6a1c` (5 × 2 bytes = 10 bytes). Selection 4 = LEAVE (exits loop). The other 4 selections call into the 4 chest-action handlers (0x175f, 0x2582, 0x23b5, 0x3406 — exact 1:1 mapping unverified without runtime trace).

evidence.details: Body: `cVar1 = *(char*)(param_1 + 0x27); if (cVar1 == 0) *0x5024 = 0xffff; else if (cVar1 == 1) *0x5024 = 0; else if (cVar1 == 2) *0x5024 = 1; wtrea_select_trap_type(param_1); ... open windows ... draw menu cells ... do { local_a = wtrea_grid_menu_picker(local_c, 0x1451, local_22, 2, 1, 10, 3, 5, 0, 0x4e05); } while (4 < local_a); (*(code*)*(undefined2*)(local_a*2 + -0x6a1c))()`. The `-0x6a1c` is signed (= 0x95e4 unsigned 16-bit) — CS-relative jumptable address. The 5 actions are dispatched by index 0..4. Functions called only via this dispatch (no intra-overlay direct callers): 0x175f, 0x19e5, 0x23b5, 0x2582, 0x3406.

findings.claim: `wtrea_inventory_insert` (0x401f) is the chest-→-character inventory insert. Same 10-main + 12-overflow layout as wmnpc/wpcvw. Source item flags translated: bit 0x08 → 0x04 (cursed-unidentified), bit 0x04 → 0x08 (cursed-identified), bit 0x10 → 0x10, bit 0x20 → 0x20, bit 0x02 → 0x40 (class-locked / cursed-on-equip). Returns 0xffff on full. Quantity merged with `< 0xfb` cap for stackable items.

evidence.details: After main+overflow scan with stackable-merge: `*(iVar5+0x4428) = item_id; *(iVar5+0x442c) = item_type; *(iVar5+0x442d) = id_mark; *(iVar5+0x442a) = misc_word; *(iVar5+0x442e) += quantity_rolled; *(iVar5+0x442f) = 0; if (local_15 & 8) *(iVar5+0x442f) |= 4; if (local_15 & 4) *(iVar5+0x442f) |= 8; if (local_15 & 0x10) *(iVar5+0x442f) |= 0x10; if (local_15 & 0x20) *(iVar5+0x442f) |= 0x20; if (local_15 & 2) *(iVar5+0x442f) |= 0x40;`. Total inventory weight recomputed via `inventory_item_weight_lookup` (0x3fc0) on each slot. Cursed-flag bit translation matches wpcvw's findings — chest items can be cursed by class (0x40 = class-locked = unequippable without remove-curse) or by default 'identified-cursed' (0x01) etc.

findings.claim: `wtrea_loot_distribution_ui` (0x43ee, 1583 bytes) handles the chest-contents-give UI. Opens 2 windows (item-list + item-detail), iterates *0x5266 items, lets player navigate with L/R cursor + ENTER, calls `wtrea_pick_party_member_target` (0x10e5) for target, then `wtrea_inventory_insert` (0x401f) to add. On full-inventory: plays sound 0x4970 + msg 0x13f4. Items left behind get *0x5274[i] = 1 flagged for the 'leave-behind' sound 0x49cd at end.

evidence.details: Body: opens local_e + local_1e windows (item-list + detail); paints UI grid via `wtrea_putchar_at_with_attr` (0x4345) calls; main loop `do { for local_4 in 0..*0x5266: render item row; cursor input via wtrea_grid_menu_picker; if ENTER: call wtrea_pick_party_member_target (FUN_10e5) with msg 0x13f1; if target chosen and item still available: call wtrea_inventory_insert (FUN_401f); on -1 (inventory full): play sound 0x4970; else FUN_436e (wtrea_loot_pile_pop_item); } while (*0x5266 > 0);`. The final 'any-items-left-behind' check: `for local_4 in 0..*0x5266: if *(local_4*2 + 0x5274) == 1: iVar2 = 1; if (iVar2 == 1): play sound 0x49cd ('leave-behind' tone)`. Confirmed by the modal-msg structure and ENTER/ESC handling identical to wpcvw's drop UI.

findings.claim: `wtrea_render_3d_view` (0x6c8f, 2192 bytes) is wtrea's embedded copy of the 3D dungeon wall renderer (mirroring wmnpc's 0xa8ca). Same wall-bitmap access pattern at *0x4faa+0x43a/+0x49a, same facing rotation via *0x4f9a, same multi-cell forward traversal. Renders 4 cells × N directions with the 14 wall-render dispatchers (scene_visit_*). Stores per-frame visibility data in *0x52cc..*0x5310 grid. The *0x363c sub-state distinguishes modes (0/4/5/10/12 — same as wmnpc).

evidence.details: 0x6c8f body: reads `local_4 = *0x4fa4; local_6 = *0x4fa2; local_8 = *0x4fa0; local_a = *0x4f9e; local_c = *0x4f9c;` (5 wall-state params); calls `FUN_f130 (a sprite-render thunk)` to initialize; `getbit_test(*0x4faa + 0x43a, ...)` for wall check; switch on *0x363c (0/4/5/10/12 ≡ wmnpc's set); else: memsets multiple visibility-grids at 0x52cc, 0x5284, 0x52ec; calls `scene_apply_facing_rotation` (0x595f) to step forward; loop `while (*0x5282 < *0x5460)` with `scene_visit_forward_cell` (0x59e0). All wall constants are HARDCODED inline — same set as wmnpc and wmaze.

findings.claim: `skill_train_chance_increment` (0x14f2) is the skill-training primitive. Reads skill_byte at `param_1*0x1b0 + param_2 + 0x451c`. If skill < 100: roll rng(current_skill); if roll <= level * param_3: skill += 1. So skills train more reliably at low values (small skill = lower rng range), and faster for characters with higher level. param_3 = class-modifier multiplier (3 for Thief disarm, 2 for Ninja/Bard, etc.). Used by wtrea after successful disarm.

evidence.details: `iVar2 = param_1*0x1b0 + param_2; if (*(byte*)(iVar2+0x451c) < 100) { iVar2 = rng(*(byte*)(iVar2+0x451c)); if (iVar2 <= *(int*)(param_1*0x1b0+0x440c) * param_3) { *(char*)(iVar2_recomputed+0x451c) += 1; } }`. The +0x451c offset is the skill array base; param_2 selects which skill (e.g., 0xf for disarm). The level multiplier in param_3 makes high-level characters train faster, and the skill < 100 cap means skills max out at 100. The rng(current_skill) check makes early progression rapid but late progression slow (a 90-skill needs roll <= level*mul on rng(90)).

findings.claim: `wtrea_action_open_or_inspect` (0x23b5) computes 'open' success probabilities with stronger class scaling: `local_4 = thief_skill_byte/10 + level/5 - dungeon_depth + class_bonus_a`; `local_6 = thief_skill_byte/2 + level/5 + class_bonus_b - dungeon_depth * class_factor`. Class 3 (Thief): a=5, b=0x32 (50), factor=2. Class 4/6/13: a=3, b=0x23 (35), factor=3/2. Other: a=1, b=0xf (15), factor=1. Then calls `wtrea_progressive_trap_reveal` (0x21c9) with these as parameters to reveal trap letters.

evidence.details: Body: `iVar3 = *(int*)(param_2*0x1b0+0x440c)/5; if (6 < iVar3) iVar3 = 6; if (class == 3) { local_4 = (skill/10 + iVar3) - depth + 5; local_6 = skill/2 + iVar3 + 0x32 + depth*-2; } else if (class in {4,6,13}) { local_4 = (skill/10 + iVar3) - depth + 3; local_6 = (skill/2 + iVar3 + 0x23) - (depth * 3) / 2; } else { local_4 = (skill/10 + iVar3) - depth + 1; local_6 = (skill/2 + iVar3 + 0xf) - depth; } clamp(local_4, min=1); clamp(local_6, 5..0x5f); wtrea_progressive_trap_reveal(param_1, param_2, local_4, local_6);`. So OPEN doesn't directly disarm — it calls into the same reveal mechanic as INSPECT, but with more aggressive parameters.

findings.claim: `wtrea_action_apply_trap_damage` (0x175f) is the trap-fires damage handler. engineering_notes_candidates.title: Wiz6 thief disarm: chest-difficulty is a hard wall, and misidentification = critical fail
engineering_notes_candidates.summary: The disarm formula in `wtrea_action_disarm_trap` is `score = thief_skill/2 + dex/2 + level - dungeon_depth*2`, with Thief class getting +dex*3 and Ninja/Bard +dex*2 on top. The score caps at 95% (0x5f) so a maxed Thief at any depth still has a guaranteed 5% chance to miss. The brutal part is the critical-fail branch: roll > 100 - (100-score)/3 triggers the trap automatically. At score 50, that means roll > 100 - 50/3 = 84 → 16% critical-fail rate. But the FORMULA never even rolls if the player MISIDENTIFIED the trap type from the displayed list of bit-set candidates — picking the wrong trap is treated identically to a critical fail. Combined with the per-attempt nature of the progressive-reveal INSPECT mechanic, players who try to disarm without exhaustive inspection are essentially gambling. Players who memorize trap-name patterns from prior runs have a huge edge; players who don't get punished disproportionately. This is the kind of 'skill expression' Wiz6 was built around — and it's also why third-party trainers for Wiz6 universally include trap-list overrides.

engineering_notes_candidates.title: TPK treasure forfeit: dying on the kill-the-last-monster moment loses the loot you just earned
engineering_notes_candidates.summary: The treasure-roll handler at `wtrea_run_loot_rolls` checks the alive-party-count AFTER rolling the loot but BEFORE distributing it. If zero are alive (because the final monster's counterattack killed the last alive character), the function writes `*0x363a=8` to trigger the graveyard handler and exits — never running the per-character XP/gold/item distribution. So the rolled treasure (which is already determined by RNG) is effectively wasted. This is a notable quirk because in many CRPGs the post-combat treasure is granted regardless of post-kill survival; in Wiz6 you have to keep someone alive long enough to claim it. Practical implication: don't engage suicidally aggressive 'last-stand' tactics on the final enemy of a known-loot encounter — keep at least one weak member alive to receive the spoils.

engineering_notes_candidates.title: The Wiz6 trap-name reveal: word-puzzle with persistent decoy state
engineering_notes_candidates.summary: `wtrea_select_trap_type` picks the actual trap (1 of 16) at chest-spawn time and stores the name string at *0x50de. Each INSPECT or successful OPEN call invokes `wtrea_progressive_trap_reveal` which (a) marks already-displayed decoys as 'real' if they match a letter in the actual name (via `rng(100) > 0x32` + skill check), and (b) appends NEW letters — either from the actual name (color 6 = white) or random A-Z decoys (color 12 = dark). Crucially, the display buffer at *0x51bc PERSISTS across multiple inspect attempts within a single chest interaction, so investing multiple INSPECTs into one chest gradually reveals more of the trap name. Combined with the trap-name table at MSG.DBS +0x14b4 being a finite set of 16 names (POISON_GAS, ALARM, MAGE_BLASTER, etc.), an experienced player can identify a trap from just 2-3 colored letters. This is the Calfo / Priests-Prayer / Wizard's-Eye mechanic in pure form: not a random check, but a structured information game. Newer CRPGs almost universally replaced this with a pass/fail roll, losing the cleverness.

engineering_notes_candidates.title: Chest spells are SCHOOL-FILTERED by what you know, so spellbook breadth matters more than total spell count
engineering_notes_candidates.summary: When the player picks SPELL on a chest, `wtrea_action_cast_chest_spell` opens a 6-cell SCHOOL selector. For each school cell, `wtrea_filter_known_spells_in_school` scans all 82 spell IDs and returns only those where (a) the spell's school-byte matches AND (b) the character's spell-known bitmap at +0x4570 has that bit set. So a Bishop or Sage with broad spellbook can engage all 6 schools, while a single-class caster may only see 1-2 school options. Power level (1..6) is capped at (caster_level - spell_base_level + 1), so even after picking a spell you need at least 1 caster-level above the spell's base level to cast at all, and 6 over to maximize damage/range. Mana is per-school (32-bit per school × 6 = 24 bytes of mana state), so spending Priest mana doesn't drain Mage mana — schools are independent budgets. The combination means: a level-20 single-class Mage casting their best spells at chests is more efficient PER ENCOUNTER than a level-12 Bishop, but the Bishop has more SITUATIONAL flexibility. This is why Wiz6 'best party' guides always recommend at least one breadth class.
